title: dedicated-autoscaler-tokenbucket-smoothing-and-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Improved token-bucket smoothing in the dedicated autoscaler to reduce sudden scale-ups; added new utilization metrics and Grafana dashboards; no user-facing API changes.
description: Context: Dedicated fleets occasionally observe sharp scale-ups when a transient burst of requests arrives, which increases cost and churn. This change implements token-bucket smoothing to dampen short-lived spikes and improves utilization reporting so SREs can reason about burst behavior. Summary: 1) Add a token-bucket smoothing layer configurable per-fleet with two knobs (smoothing_window_ms and max_burst_tokens). 2) Adjust autoscaler decision logic to consult smoothed token rate before triggering scale-out. 3) Emit new metrics: autoscaler.smoothed_rate, autoscaler.burst_tokens, autoscaler.scale_decision_cause and per-fleet 95th/99th utilization histograms. 4) Ship Grafana dashboard and alerting templates. Motivation: Reduce oscillation and unnecessary GPU startups while preserving throughput guarantees for sustained load. Linear/JIRA: ENG-4218 (autoscaler smoothing design), ENG-4290 (utilization reporting), SUP-2045 (customer incident referencing burst). Testing: unit tests for smoothing math and edge cases, deterministic integration test that injects bursts, load test on staging cluster with a 3-day run. Rollout: feature gated by fleet config (smoothing_enabled=false by default), staged rollout to 10% of fleets for 48h, full rollout after monitoring. Config knobs and defaults: smoothing_window_ms=5000, max_burst_tokens=1000, decision_threshold_delta=0.15. Backwards compatibility: none required for API; config additions are optional. Checklist: - [x] design doc updated - [x] unit tests added - [x] integration tests added - [x] dashboard+alerts included - [x] changelog/release notes added - [x] staged rollout plan documented
